name: Box jumps

card.summary: A plyometric exercise of jumping onto a raised box that trains explosive leg power, feeding an athletic, muscular lower body.
card.note: High-impact; injury risk rises with poor technique or too much height.

quick.overview:
A box jump is a plyometric exercise in which the lifter jumps from the floor onto a box or platform. It trains explosive power in the quadriceps, glutes and calves and is used by athletes and gym-goers who want a powerful, athletic lower body.

Plyometric training is associated with gains in power and jumping performance, and studies have measured how box jumps compare with other plyometrics in muscle activation.
quick.how: Box jumps are done in short sets with full recovery, usually as part of a lower-body or conditioning session, on a stable box. Many programs place them early in a workout when the lifter is fresh, and progress by box height or by combining with strength work.
quick.risks: Plyometrics create large impact forces and carry injury risk; Wikipedia notes participants should build strength and technique first. In CrossFit contexts, a meta-analysis found urinary incontinence prevalence of about 32% in female participants, with jumping-type exercises among those associated.

lead: A box jump is a plyometric exercise in which an athlete jumps onto and off a raised box, usually 45 cm or higher according to Wikipedia. [1] People use it to build explosive leg power and an athletic lower body. [1][2]

Plyometrics use the stretch-shortening cycle, and Wikipedia credits Soviet scientist Yuri Verkhoshansky with the original shock method built around depth jumps, with the term popularized by Fred Wilt. [1] A 23-athlete study compared motor unit activation of the quadriceps, hamstrings and gastrocnemius across plyometric exercises, including box jumps. [2]
A 12-week randomized trial in preadolescent soccer players used box jumps among its plyometric exercises and tested sprint, jump and power outcomes. [3]

chain: Stretch-shortening cycle loads quads, glutes and calves
Greater power and muscle tone in the legs
angle.text: Box jumps train power and are used in routines for sprint, jump and leg development, which contribute to an athletic physique.

paras: Plyometrics are maximum-intensity explosive exercises using the stretch-shortening cycle. [1] Box jumps are listed as jumping onto a box of 45 cm or higher. [1]

Plyometrics are used to improve power, strength and jumping performance, and in team sports combined with neuromuscular training have been shown to reduce lower-limb injuries. [1] A randomized trial of boys aged about 10 found plyometric training twice a week for 12 weeks, including box jumps, was assessed for speed and power. [3]

Wikipedia states plyometrics involve increased injury risk due to the forces generated. [1] A 2022 meta-analysis found 32.1% prevalence of urinary incontinence among female CrossFit practitioners, higher in women over 35 and with prior pregnancies. [4]

An electromyography study of 23 athletes compared plyometric intensity across exercises including box jumps. [2] A 12-week randomized controlled trial in 45 preadolescent soccer players included box jumps in its plyometric protocol. [3] These studies tested the plyometric categories rather than box jumps alone.
